justification: Presentation is clearly ahead of what ranks for '4 pillars of oop'. The pages I re-read this round have no runnable output panels, at most one diagram, no exercises and no phone-aware code. This page has one consistent billing domain, every program paired with its output panel, two figures that fit a 390 px column at about 11 px text (viewBox 360 wide) and are correct in light and dark, a red 'Does not compile: CS0122' block, five exercises spread through the article with collapsed solutions and no output given away, three earned callouts (note, In .NET, exercise), one H1, question-style H2s with specific H3s, and a 15-item source list with inline numbered cites. Round 1 held the score at 8.2 for phone clipping and a three-column table. Both are fixed: the longest csharp line is now 41 columns (eight lines, and only a trailing semicolon or paren sits under the fade; the earlier operative clips `: Plan`, `12m, 5` and `- _paid` are gone), the opening table is two columns and fully visible at 390 px, the throws block now has an output panel, Figure 2's arrow leaves the pointer row and lands on the table with numbered badges 2 and 3 on the slot row, Figure 1's desc no longer promises a blocked-write drawing, and a lead-in sentence tells the phone reader to read three methods and skip the driver in the long Invoice listing. I found no blocker or major on this pass. What keeps it from 9: the closing section leans on text that lives only in a collapsed solution, one code block loses keyword highlighting, Figure 1's label sits against an arrowhead, the two longest listings are still several phone screens of unbroken code, and the beginner badge sits on a page that ends in JIT devirtualization and virtual stub dispatch. All are small, mostly one-line fixes. Round-1 technical blocker (invariant stated as 'exactly when' paid) is fixed: the prose now says a paid invoice owes nothing and an issued one still owes something, and Figure 1 says 'Paid owes nothing; Issued owes something'. The misquoted spec sentence is now a verbatim attributed quote, and the primary-constructor caveat is in the Note callout. The round-1 adsense major about level versus body is half resolved: each pillar now opens with a plain definition, but level stays beginner with empty prerequisites (minor here).

issues.location: H2 'How do the four fit together?', first paragraph (md line ~928), which mentions Plan.PriceFor 'from the last exercise' and 'each plan fills in Compute'
issues.problem: Compute exists only inside the collapsed solution of Exercise 3 (md lines ~810-835). A reader who did not open the solution meets an undefined member name in the synthesis paragraph, and the shape that paragraph describes (a PriceFor that checks non-negativity, then calls a protected abstract member) is not visible on the page. The section that should tie the four together therefore depends on hidden content, and it is only two short paragraphs, so it reads thinner than the rest.
issues.fixLooksLike: Make the paragraph stand alone: say in one clause what the exercise-3 shape is ('a public non-virtual PriceFor that checks the result and calls a protected abstract member') or show the 8-10 line skeleton in a short visible block, then use the names from it. Optionally give the section one visible artifact (a small table: pillar | what it guards | where it appears in Invoice and Plan) so it is not only prose.

issues.location: Code highlighting in the block that starts `Plan plan = new PromoPlan(price: 29m, credit: 40m);` (desktop-light part 12, mobile-dark part 17)
issues.problem: After the `record Usage(int Seats);` line, keywords in the same block lose their colour: `abstract class Plan`, `sealed`, `public abstract`, `public override` render in plain text colour while `decimal`, `record`, `static void`, `throw new` stay coloured. The same keywords colour correctly in the other blocks on the page (Invoice, plans), so this block looks half-styled in both themes.
issues.fixLooksLike: Find why the highlighter state drops there (possibly the record line followed by a class with a primary constructor) and fix it in the shell's C# grammar or code component so keyword modifiers colour uniformly. Append to docs/INTEGRATOR_REQUESTS.md.

issues.location: Front matter `level: beginner`, `prerequisites: []`, versus the sections 'What the runtime does with plan.PriceFor(usage)', 'What does a virtual call cost?' and the 'In .NET' callout
issues.problem: The badge under the title says BEGINNER, but the page discusses the heap, method tables, slots, guarded devirtualization and virtual stub dispatch, and uses records, primary constructors and collection expressions. The round-1 adsense critic raised this as a major; the plain per-pillar definitions now cover the vocabulary half, but the badge and empty prerequisites are unchanged, and nothing tells a reader who trusts the badge that the runtime half is optional.
issues.fixLooksLike: Either set level to intermediate with a prerequisite on classes and objects basics, or keep beginner and add one sentence at the start of the runtime section saying it is optional on a first read and the argument continues at 'What does inheritance cost?'.

issues.location: Monospace digits in code and output (for example 344, 44, 245m in the first two listings and their outputs, all screenshots)
issues.problem: In the stack `ui-monospace, Cascadia Code, Cascadia Mono, Consolas...` the digit 4 renders with an open top on this machine, so 44 and 344 look like uu and 3uu at code size. The article's numbers carry the argument (245 vs 344 vs 44 owed), so this costs readability. It depends on the reader's installed font, so it is a shell decision, not an article defect.
issues.fixLooksLike: Consider listing a monospace with a closed 4 first (Consolas or Menlo before Cascadia), or ship one webfont for code so numerals look the same everywhere.
